questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Costa Rica?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Costa Rica article.

questions.proof: Its capital and largest city is San José.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Costa Rica?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Costa Rica on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Costa Rica article.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Costa Rica?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Pre-Columbian period” part of the Costa Rica article.

questions.proof: Most of the indigenous population was absorbed into the Spanish colony.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Costa Rica never fought for independence from _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “independence”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Independence” part of the Costa Rica article.

questions.proof: Costa Rica never fought for independence from Spain.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “On September 15, 1821, after the last Spanish defeat in the Mexican War of Independence (1810–21), the authorities in _____ declared the independence of all of Central America.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “declared”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Independence” part of the Costa Rica article.

questions.proof: On September 15, 1821, after the last Spanish defeat in the Mexican War of Independence (1810–21), the authorities in Guatemala declared the independence of all of Central America.
